_readme: Finance's part of the portal's feature catalogue and of the per-org backfill. The portal migration loads this; Finance does not run it.
features -> one row each for core.features (key, service_key = 'finance', name, description, requires, default_on).
backfill.orgs -> core.org_features rows with enabled = true, per org SLUG (slugs are the same in every environment; org ids are not).

backfill.also_on -> orgs that cannot be listed by name. Each rule is a query returning org ids; every org it returns gets the listed features enabled = true. Run these inside the migration, against the data as it is that day.
Everything not named by either gets no row, which reads as the feature's default_on (false for all three below) - so every org sees exactly what it sees today.

'Today' is: finance.vehicles / rent / emi on for vehicle accounts (finance.org_settings.sells_vehicles, or a business name that reads 'Deeva Auto'), off for everyone else. Nothing else in Finance is a feature (see FEATURE-INVENTORY.md).
finance.jageer is not here: it lives in the portal database (public.finance_apply_jageer_*) and belongs in the portal's own list.

features.name: Vehicle accounts
features.description: Names the vehicle on bills, ledgers and reports, adds a Model No. to purchase bills, and splits Stock (what is in hand) from Inventory (every vehicle).

features.name: Rent
features.description: Give vehicles out on rent by the day. The daily rent is posted to the renter's ledger and counts as income.

features.name: EMI
features.description: Sell or buy vehicles on monthly instalments, with a plan and a schedule for each vehicle.

also_on.why: Vehicle accounts: the old switch, finance.org_settings.sells_vehicles, and the business-name match the app used before it existed. Rent and EMI were shown to exactly these.
also_on.org_ids_sql: select org_id from finance.org_settings where sells_vehicles union select id from core.organizations where name ~* '\ydee?va\s+auto\y'

also_on.why: An org that already has rentals keeps the Rent page that holds them, even if it never had the menu item (the page was reachable by address).
